LESSON: MULTIPLICATION (8

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.4: Multiplication (8

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Multiplication (8. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: When can you use multiplication in real life? 2. 2. How can you create patterns involving multiplication?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. multiply up to a two-digit number by multiples of 10 in different situations,
2. multiply up to a two-digit number by two-digit number with and without regrouping,
3. multiply up to a two digit number by 100 in different situations,
4. estimate products by rounding off numbers to the nearest 10 with product not exceeding 1,000, e) d) create patterns involving multiplication with product not exceeding 100, f) e) appreciate application of multiplication of numbers in real-life situations. SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market in your county, count 10 mangoes. Put them in 2 groups of 5. That is sorting and grouping.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row. Write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and your parent gives you 5 more, you have 12 shillings. That is addition.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Multiplication (8.
2. Explain Multiplication (8 to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Try this activity: team up with peers to multiply two-digit numbers by multiples of 10 using number cards or charts,
4. Show that you can: multiply up to a two-digit number by multiples of 10 in different situations,
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Multiplication (8. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: When can you use multiplication in real life? 2. 2. How can you create patterns involving multiplication?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Team up with peers to multiply two-digit numbers by multiples of 10 using number cards or charts,
2. Team up with others to multiply up to a two-digit number by two- digit number with and without regrouping using counters and prepare a corresponding multiplication chart,
3. Share tasks while generating patterns involving multiplication with products not exceeding 100 and prepare multiplication charts using locally available materials,
